meta.parties: Senanayake v. Selastina Hamine Et Al

rules.statement: A grantor who has granted an undivided eastern portion of land in extent 2 acres cannot claim on a partition that his grant is to be treated exactly as though it was a grant of a divided 2 acres. The court will endeavor to give effect to the intention implied by the use of such a word by assigning to the shareholder a portion in the direction indicated.
rules.supporting_quote: "But, I think, it is clear that defendant cannot have intended to sell 2 acres out of lot B, because a glance at the plan will show that 2 acres extent to the east of lot B would include the defendant's residing house. Moreover, plaintiffs argument from the value of the land as recited in the deed is worthless, because the value recited there is admittedly fictitious. Hence, since defendant did not intend to sell from lot B, it must be from lot C, and it certainly accords best with the wording of the deed, since lot C stretches further east than the rest of the land."
